high.title: Peso Tumbles to Over Three-Week Low
high.summary: The Philippine Peso depreciated sharply by 26.1 centavos on Wednesday, closing at P61.621 against the US Dollar — its weakest level in over three weeks, last seen on June 8 when it settled at P61.69. The sell-off was driven by two concurrent forces: hawkish US Federal Reserve expectations, which are strengthening dollar demand broadly across emerging market FX, and persistent geopolitical uncertainty stemming from the ongoing Middle East conflict, which is bolstering safe-haven dollar flows. The move signals a potential re-test of recent cycle lows for the Peso. For FX traders, the break below P61.40 support is technically significant and opens the door to further downside toward the P61.70–P62.00 range if US rate expectations remain elevated. Bond investors should monitor whether sustained Peso weakness prompts the BSP to reassess its own easing posture or intervene in FX markets. Watch upcoming US economic data and Fed communications closely, as these will be the primary external drivers for PHP direction in the near term.

high.title: TDF Yield Climbs on Hawkish BSP, Fed
high.summary: The BSP's 7-day Term Deposit Facility (TDF) auction saw yields rise amid hawkish monetary policy expectations from both the BSP and the US Federal Reserve, with tenders reaching P146.927 billion against a P110 billion offer — confirming the facility remains heavily oversubscribed. The uptick in TDF yields is a critical signal for the short end of the Philippine rates curve, suggesting markets are pricing out near-term BSP rate cuts and potentially pricing in a more prolonged hold. For bond investors, this implies upward pressure on short-duration government securities, which could steepen or flatten the curve depending on long-end behavior. The strong oversubscription also reflects ample domestic liquidity being parked at the BSP, a dynamic worth monitoring for its implications on credit growth and government bond demand. This development directly complements the Peso weakness story — a hawkish BSP stance may help provide a floor for PHP, but it simultaneously signals tighter financial conditions domestically.

high.title: Bond Yields Go Down as Oil's Drop Eases Inflation Worries
high.summary:
The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) achieved a full award of its reissued 7-year T-bond auction, borrowing the planned P30 billion at a lower-than-expected average yield. The auction attracted strong demand, with total bids reaching P65.135 billion — more than 2x oversubscribed — bringing the outstanding volume for this bond series to P243 billion. The key driver was a decline in global oil prices, linked to progress on a Middle East peace deal, which reduced near-term inflation expectations and encouraged investors to accept lower yields. **For bond investors**, this signals a constructive near-term backdrop for Philippine government securities (GovSecs), with demand robust and the yield curve potentially biasing lower on the belly. **For FX traders**, easing inflation fears reduce pressure on the BSP to maintain a hawkish stance, which could temper PHP carry support but is broadly peso-neutral to slightly positive on improved fiscal optics. Watch for the June CPI print and next BSP policy meeting for confirmation of the disinflationary trend.

---

medium.title: BSP Says Wholesale CBDCs Can Reduce Transaction Costs, Lags
medium.summary:
The BSP highlighted findings from Project Agila, its wholesale CBDC (wCBDC) pilot, identifying cross-border payments — including OFW remittances and institutional transfers — and financial securities settlement as priority use cases. For an international fund manager, this is a medium-term structural development: if wCBDCs streamline remittance flows, it could enhance the predictability and efficiency of a key USD/PHP FX support mechanism, as OFW remittances are a major source of dollar inflows for the Philippines. Securities settlement improvements could also reduce friction for foreign portfolio investors transacting in Philippine bonds and equities. While still at the pilot stage, this initiative reflects the BSP's forward-looking approach to financial infrastructure and warrants monitoring as it progresses toward potential implementation.

---

medium.title: PHL Posts Net Hot Money Inflow in May
medium.summary: Foreign portfolio investments (FPI) registered with the BSP swung to a net inflow of $232.46 million in May, reversing two consecutive months of net outflows, signaling a recovery in risk appetite toward Philippine assets. However, the figure remains significantly below the $600.77 million net inflow recorded in the same month a year earlier, suggesting the rebound is modest and fragile. For PHP and PSEi traders, the return of hot money flows is a near-term positive, providing FX demand support for the peso and potential equity market tailwinds. The sustainability of these inflows will be highly sensitive to global risk sentiment, Fed policy signals, and domestic macro developments — particularly inflation and GDP growth trajectory. Monitor June FPI data and BSP reserve figures for confirmation of a sustained trend reversal.

medium.title: Philippine GDP Likely Grew 2.6% in Q2, Says UA&P
medium.summary: UA&P estimates Philippine Q2 2026 GDP growth slowed to 2.6%, weighed down by elevated inflation and weakening domestic demand, raising concerns about the broader economic recovery momentum. While UA&P notes early signs of recovery, the constrained outlook has implications for BSP's rate path — a weaker growth print could reinforce the case for policy easing, which would be bearish for PHP carry but supportive for bond prices. For PSEi investors, sluggish GDP growth may pressure corporate earnings expectations, particularly in consumer-facing sectors. This estimate will be watched closely ahead of the official PSA GDP release; a significant miss versus government targets could trigger a reassessment of Philippines sovereign risk and capital flow dynamics.

medium.title: NCR Retail Price Growth Slows to 2-Month Low in May
medium.summary: Metro Manila's General Retail Price Index (GRPI) rose 4.0% year-on-year in May, easing from 4.5% in April — the softest pace in two months — largely on declining prices of mineral fuels and lubricants. While this is a retail-level indicator rather than the headline CPI, the deceleration is directionally consistent with a broader easing inflation narrative in the Philippines. For PHP and rate traders, moderating price pressures provide additional room for the BSP to maintain or extend its easing cycle without reigniting inflation fears. Bond investors should note that a sustained softening in price indices supports the case for lower long-end yields. Watch for the official May national CPI print and any BSP commentary on the inflation path, as these will be the more decisive data points for near-term policy rate expectations.

medium.title: Philippine Shares Rebound as Investors Pick Up Bargains
medium.summary: The PSEi recovered 0.53% (+32.09 points) to close at 6,069.26 on Wednesday, clawing back a portion of the prior session's sharp 1.56% decline, as bargain hunters stepped in at lower valuations. Sentiment was additionally supported by optimism surrounding US-Iran diplomatic negotiations, which helped ease regional risk aversion. The rebound is technically constructive but remains fragile given the still-uncertain geopolitical backdrop. Foreign participation and net buying/selling data will be key to watch — sustained foreign inflows would be supportive of the PHP alongside equity market stabilization.

medium.title: Philippine Stocks Drop on Uncertainty Over US-Iran Talks
medium.summary: The PSEi fell 1.56% (-96.24 points) to close at 6,037.17 on Tuesday, pressured by profit-taking amid geopolitical uncertainty surrounding US-Iran negotiations and a perceived weakening of the local economic outlook. The broader All Shares Index also declined by 1.0% (-33.67 points) to 3,319.29. The dual headwinds of offshore geopolitical risk and domestic macro concerns are a reminder of the PSEi's vulnerability to sentiment-driven swings. A sustained risk-off mood in equities could spill over into mild PHP softness via foreign portfolio outflows — a key channel for international fund managers to monitor.
